articles.title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game
articles.summary: Kane double helps Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0. Dieter Müller’s record of 129 games had stood since 1977. Harry Kane smashed the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club.
body: Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and, with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game, a new record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival in 2023 Kane had been averaging a Bundesliga goal every 78.5 minutes and has now scored 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last term.
He blasted home a 39th-minute penalty to take the record before nodding in a Michael Olise cross early in the second half to send Bayern top of the table before the other weekend matches.
The feat stole the spotlight from Olise, who scored his first Bayern hat-trick, and Jamal Musiala, who also scored a goal worthy of winning any game.

“I’m very proud to have now scored 100 and 101 Bundesliga goals. I haven’t been around that long. I’ve loved every second of it,” Kane told Sky Germany. “With Michael, Lucho [Luis Díaz] and Jamal I naturally get chances and today was no exception.
points: Kane double helps Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0.

articles.title: Keely Hodgkinson shows off Catwoman style to steal Athlos London event
articles.summary: Briton destroys 800m field in hooded black bodysuit. Mill Hill event more like a rave than an athletics meeting. Athlos arrived in London promising that its all-female spin on athletics would provide a radical departure from the status quo.
body: Throughout the two-hour event, the bassline from the aptly named DJ Trauma carried enough force to make eardrums bleed. The stadium PA’s dial appeared to be permanently stuck on Spinal Tap’s 11. And those who successfully scanned a barcode were then shown dancing and waving on a giant screen.

But the youngish crowd largely lapped it up. As Hodgkinson was introduced, the stadium MC told the cheering crowd: “Wait until she comes around the corner, she looks bad, bad, bad. In a custom Nike suit, Keely Hodgkinson!”
Soon the roars had become even louder. Athletics sometimes resembles a vicarage tea party. This was more like a rave. Mill Hill has surely never seen anything like it.

Afterwards, the Paris Olympic 800m champion insisted that the suit and its aerodynamic design, which also contained openings for her sunglasses and ponytail, had given her an edge. But she could have been running in a thick duffle coat and she would still have won the $65,000 first prize and Tiffany crown with ease.

articles.title: Hodgkinson powers to Athlos win in speed suit
articles.summary: Keely Hodgkinson powers to victory in a full-body speed suit before being presented with a Tiffany & Co crown as Athlos makes its London debut.
body: Keely Hodgkinson powered to victory in a custom-made full-body speed suit before being presented with a Tiffany & Co crown as Athlos made its London debut.
Hodgkinson was greeted by loud cheers as she emerged on to a stage and revealed the all-black aerodynamic outfit at the third staging of the all-female athletics meet.

The 24-year-old ensured she ended a mixed year with a dominant 800m victory in front of a sellout home crowd at StoneX Stadium, bursting clear on the back straight and crossing the line in one minute 56.40 seconds.
Speaking about the outfit, Hodgkinson told BBC Sport: "This has been like a year in the making. It's a mixture of fashion and speed and science all coming together for maybe the future of athletics.

articles.title: Brentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half display
articles.summary: Those early-season thoughts that Chelsea might be the team best-placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look extremely over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure…
body: At the final whistle, Keith Andrews tipped his head back and roared at the sky, celebrating Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938. They remain unbeaten, coherent and disciplined, and moved up to third in the table. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flail in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction. “It was a performance I felt was bubbling,” said Andrews. “I could see it in the players’ eyes over the last two days. They were very focused, very determined.”

Such is the state of perpetual flux at Chelsea that the usual homilies about the benefits of stability always seem a little redundant when applied to them. With 11 new signings this summer maintaining the sense of the club as a trading hub, learning the names of everybody in the dressing room has probably been a greater priority than worrying too much about boardroom wrangling. But, still, their first game since Todd Boehly and Mark Walter agreed to sell their 12.8% stake in the club to the major shareholder Clearlake Capital felt significant. At the very least, a more harmonious boardroom should be beneficial.

articles.title: Women’s Super League: Lauren Hemp hits double as Manchester City see off lively Liverpool
articles.summary: Manchester City continued their winning start to the new Women’s Super League season but the defending champions needed a 90th-minute own goal from Grace Fisk to help them edge past an ever-improving Liverpool side after an entertaining game in which Lauren Hemp scored twice.
body: Fisk inadvertently turned Grace Clinton’s dangerous cross into her own net to put City 3-2 up and then – with Liverpool searching for an equaliser and committing players forward deep in stoppage time – Hemp added another on the counterattack to make it 4-2 and widen the margin of victory, but that slightly masked how well the visitors had played.
Gareth Taylor – against his former side – will have taken significant encouragement from his Liverpool team’s performance, on a night when they made the league leaders dig deep.

“Playing that way, we believe we’ll win a lot of games this season,” Taylor told Sky Sports, as he praised his team’s effort. “What you saw was a more improved version of what we were towards the end of last season.”

That certainly seemed the case. Nevertheless, the result ensured that City, who had already been the only WSL side who held a 100% winning record after the opening two rounds of games and now will certainly stay top of the table for at least another week, have still not dropped any points in home league fixtures since Andrée Jeglertz took charge in the summer of 2025.

articles.title: Nick Wright doesn’t get why people think Ryan Fitzpatrick is ‘charismatic’
articles.summary: Dating back to his days as an NFL quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick has been a favorite of both the media and fans. The journeyman was a great quote for reporters and hosts, and lived up to the notion that backup quarterbacks are always the fan favorite on a team.
body: Since joining the Prime Video crew on T hursday Night Football, Fitzpatrick has remained a daring darling of the football community. The big-bearded QB was in Buffalo for the opening of Highmark Stadium, and celebrated with a traditional leap through a folding table.

It went over great in the building, but somewhere in New York City, FS1’s Nick Wright watched with bemusement. Friday on First Things First as the show aired a highlight of Fitzpatrick’s table-crash, Wright questioned the hype.
“We don’t need to promote this guy. It’s enough. He gets plenty of promotion,” Wright said.

“He made a nice career for himself. He’s rebranded from, like, the Harvard smart quarterback, which never really made sense because if you watched him play, he looked like he might not be able to add. He was just crazy reckless. He was talented, but crazy reckless. And now, just because he has a long beard and we see his chest hair, he’s charismatic? I don’t get it.”

articles.title: Oscar Collazo injured, flyweight title fight off
articles.summary: Oscar Collazo ’s jump to flyweight will have to wait. The 105 lb titleholder suffered a rib injury in training ahead of his planned October 10 challenge against WBC and WBA flyweight titleholder Ricardo Sandoval, and the fight has been scrapped for now, according to Golden Boy.
body: The Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions co-promoted event will go on, as the main event between Floyd Schofield and Lucas Bahdi, for the vacant WBA lightweight title, is still on.

“This is a fight I wanted deeply,” Collazo said in a statement. “As a boxer, I pushed for this matchup to happen because I wanted to face this challenge and because I know how much it means to everyone who has been waiting to see it. My team and I have worked with seriousness and commitment throughout this camp, preparing to the fullest to be ready for fight day.”
Collazo apologized to Sandoval and his team, and made clear he intends to reschedule the fight.

articles.title: 'Bullied' and 'out of control' - Chelsea's defensive issues laid bare
articles.summary: "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.
body: Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.
And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

articles.title: How belief of Wakefield's inner sanctum led to history-making semi-final
articles.summary: When Wakefield Trinity came back into Super League for the 2025 season, there wouldn't have been many who would have foreseen a semi-final appearance within two seasons- except those in their inner sanctum.
body: That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.
Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.
